title: How To Not Be Stressed Out This School Year https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2024/08/01/how-to-not-be-stressed-out-this-school-year/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin makes the case that stress doesn't just harm a teacher personally, it directly worsens classroom behavior by importing tension and excitability into the room, and he offers eight concrete habits for staying calm through a school year. The habits range from relying entirely on a written classroom management plan to handle misbehavior, to daily pre-school visualization, refusing to create friction through lecturing or glaring, keeping the room tidy, and practicing nasal breathing to trigger the parasympathetic nervous system. He also includes personal-life habits -- sleep, exercise, and genuinely leaving work behind at the parking lot -- as part of the same system, arguing that a chaotic personal life inevitably bleeds into a stressed teaching persona. The throughline is that a calm teacher produces a calm class, so each stress-reduction habit doubles as a behavior management strategy.
points: A stressed-out teacher reliably produces a class that is more excitable and prone to misbehavior; the two are treated as directly linked.
Letting the written classroom management plan do the disciplinary work removes the emotional burden of confrontation from the teacher.
A brief daily visualization exercise before school, imagining calm responses to any disruption, is offered as a low-effort stress-reduction habit.
Refusing to create friction with students, through lecturing, glaring, or berating, is identified as a major and controllable source of stress.
quotes: Show me a stressed-out teacher and I’ll show you students bouncing off the walls. They go hand in hand like hot weather and mosquitos.
To avoid stress, you must allow your classroom management plan to do all of the dirty work of curbing misbehavior for you.
When you refuse to create friction with students (i.e. lecturing, questioning, berating, glaring, etc.), you remove a massive amount of stress.
Forcing yourself to meditate can bring on its own stress. All you really need to do is breathe through your nose and allow your exhales to linger.
To be at your even-keeled best, you have to get away from school. As soon as you leave the parking lot, shift your focus to family, friends, and hobbies.
